fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds Into the Survey
fields.features_subheading: A product market fit survey asks users how they would feel without the product. Emergent builds it, and the app scores every reply.
fields.feature_1:
The must-have question, word for word

Emergent builds the question with its three answers in a fixed order: very, somewhat, and not disappointed. Describe the follow-ups you want, and a later prompt changes them.
fields.feature_2:
A score with the count behind it

The dashboard puts the very disappointed share beside the number of people who gave that answer. A score built on 64 replies should never read like one built on 600 replies.
fields.feature_3:
Who gets asked, and only once

The app checks each email against past respondents before it sends a link. Nobody answers twice, and a sender list filtered to recent users keeps first-week signups out.
fields.feature_4:
The score split by any answer

Add a role or plan question, and the dashboard shows the very disappointed share for each group. The segment that already loves the product stands out from the rest at a glance.
fields.feature_5:
An alert when the score moves

Set the line your team aims for. When a cohort closes above or below it, the app posts the new score to a Slack channel or emails the product lead, with the reply count.
fields.feature_6:
Code you keep on paid plans

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. Every past cohort stays in the database you own, even when you fork the survey for a second product line.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Teams, Four Readings of the Score
fields.tab_content_1:
A 4-point gap keeps Driftpine under 40%

Driftpine, a shift-scheduling app, sends its survey only to the 186 users who opened the app at least twice in the last 2 weeks. Of the 64 who answered, 23 picked very disappointed, 29 somewhat disappointed, and 12 not disappointed. That share sits 4 points under the team's 40% threshold.
fields.tab_content_2:
With 25 of 48, agency owners top the 40% threshold

Brightloom, a proposal-design tool, asks each respondent for their role before the must-have question. Across 140 replies, 41 picked very disappointed. Split by role, 25 of 48 agency owners picked it. Only 9 of 52 freelancers did, and 7 of 40 in-house designers. The team now writes its roadmap for agency owners.
fields.tab_content_3:
In Q3, 89 of 212 new users pick very disappointed

Sablecrest Routes, a route-planning app for couriers, surveys each quarter's new users and never asks anyone twice. In Q1, 61 of 197 picked very disappointed, and in Q2, 74 of 200. In Q3, 89 of 212 did, the first quarter above the 40% threshold, and the app posted the result to the #product channel in Slack.
fields.tab_content_4:
Of 57 fans, 31 came for streak reminders

Junebright, a habit-tracking app, opens its survey on the phone with one question per screen. After the must-have question, users pick their main benefit from a short list. Of the 57 who picked very disappointed, 31 chose streak reminders, 15 weekly charts, and 11 shared goals. Streak reminders lead the next release.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Product Market Fit Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a product market fit survey that scores your must-have users and shows which segment to build for.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Pull the users who have used the core of the product more than once this month, and leave out anyone who signed up days ago. Describe that group in your prompt, and Emergent builds the survey and the sender list around it.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Open with the must-have question in its standard wording. Offer three answers in this order: very disappointed, somewhat disappointed, and not disappointed. Keep the wording fixed between rounds, or this quarter's score stops lining up with the last one.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask what type of person would benefit most, the main benefit they get, and how the product could improve. Turn the main benefit question into a short list rather than open text, because a list can be counted by group.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Add a single question that splits the replies: role or plan, for example. Ask it before the must-have question. One segment question is enough for a first round, and you can add another with a follow-up prompt later.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Set the threshold and the alert
fields.howto_step_5_des: Decide which line counts as a pass for your team, such as above 40%, and where the result should go. Name the Slack channel or the person whose inbox should get each closed cohort's result.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it and wait for 40 replies
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link by email, or show it to users inside the product. Hold off on reading the score until at least 40 people have answered. With fewer replies, one person changing their answer moves the share by several points.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the replies from very disappointed users and read their roles and main benefits before anything else. Build for what they value, then survey the next quarter's new users and compare the scores side by side.

faq_plan.q: What is a product market fit survey?
faq_plan.a: A product market fit survey asks current users how they would feel if they could no longer use the product: very disappointed, somewhat disappointed, or not disappointed. The share who pick very disappointed is the score. In Sean Ellis's benchmarking, companies with strong traction almost always had more than 40% of users give that answer.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a product market fit survey?
faq_plan.a: Describe the product and the users you want to reach in a prompt to Emergent's AI survey builder. Emergent builds the questions and a dashboard that splits the score by group. Every reply is saved to a database you own, and any question can be changed with another prompt.

faq_plan.q: What product market fit survey questions should I ask after the main one?
faq_plan.a: Ask three: what type of people would most benefit from the product, what main benefit they get from it, and how it could improve for them. Superhuman asked these three right after the must-have question. Use the first answer to decide who to sell to, and the second to decide what to protect.

faq_plan.q: What goes into a product market fit survey template?
faq_plan.a: A product market fit survey template holds five parts: a segment question such as role, the must-have question, and three follow-ups on who gains most, what they value, and what to fix. Leave onboarding and support questions for a customer feedback survey. Emergent builds the template from your prompt, and you edit it by prompting again.

faq_plan.q: How many responses does a product market fit survey need?
faq_plan.a: Aim for at least 40. Superhuman's write-up puts the point where results turn directionally correct at around 40 respondents. With 40 replies, each one is worth 2.5 points of the score. Treat a change of one or two replies as noise until the count grows.

faq_plan.q: What score on a product market fit survey means you have fit?
faq_plan.a: A score above 40% very disappointed is the line Sean Ellis drew after benchmarking nearly a hundred startups. Treat it as a guide rather than a pass mark: Superhuman started below it and moved closer by narrowing its focus to the users who would be very disappointed.

faq_plan.q: Which users should I send a product market fit survey to?
faq_plan.a: Send it to people who use the product now and know what it does for them. People who only know the product from ads or a demo have nothing to miss yet, and their views fit a brand perception survey better. For active users, Sean Ellis recommended those who had used the product at least twice in the previous two weeks, and Superhuman followed that rule.

faq_plan.q: How often should you run product market fit surveys?
faq_plan.a: Run them on a fixed schedule, such as every month or every quarter, and send each round to new users only. Superhuman tracked its score weekly, monthly, and quarterly, and it never surveyed the same user twice, to keep the 40% threshold meaningful.

faq_plan.q: What should I do with somewhat disappointed answers on a product market fit survey?
faq_plan.a: Split them by main benefit. Superhuman filtered its somewhat disappointed group on the benefit its biggest fans named. It paid close attention to those who shared that benefit and set aside the users who did not.

faq_plan.q: How is a product market fit survey different from a satisfaction score?
faq_plan.a: A satisfaction score asks how happy someone was with one experience, while a product market fit survey asks how much they would miss the product if it were gone. Send a customer satisfaction survey after a support ticket or a delivery, and this one when you need to know whether the product is a must-have. Emergent builds either one from a prompt.
